The operation often called convolution in deep-learning libraries is cross-correlation: the kernel is not flipped. ReLU has derivative 0 at zero. Global pooling sends one ninth of its upstream gradient to each active map entry. Shared kernel gradients sum contributions from every window.
This is a real trainable educational CNN, not image recognition on natural photographs. The simple fixed synthetic task does not measure real-world vision performance.

What this release does, and does not do

The sidebar, responsive layouts, light/dark themes, equation renderer and reusable plots form the foundation. Browser workspaces include mathematical foundations, twelve classical supervised estimators, K-Means, data exploration, preprocessing, evaluation scalar RNN/LSTM training with full BPTT, structure discovery, optimizers and the original demonstrations.

Browser CSV/Excel import and evaluation are ready. The optional local source app adds dataset training, saved experiments, model exports and isolated Python. These require a locally running API, not the hosted page. Cloud persistence is not deployed. Planned items are not training buttons.
Remaining: educational coverage, engineering refinements and full-specification checks. Local execution is available in the source app; cloud services are not deployed.

Each layer computes z=Wa+b, then an activation. Hidden activations allow nonlinear boundaries. With no hidden layer this is logistic regression, so it cannot solve XOR. Binary cross entropy and a sigmoid output give the output delta p−y. Hidden deltas use the chain rule: transpose weights times the next delta, multiplied by the activation derivative. Full-batch gradients are averaged across training examples before weights and biases are updated.

Step decay halves the rate every 50 updates. Cosine decays to zero over the chosen update budget. Inverse time uses rate/(1+decay×step). RMSprop uses the squared-gradient decay directly; Adam additionally uses first-moment memory and bias correction.
Every optimizer or objective edit resets its state and moment accumulators. Lower the learning rate if the loss rises or updates diverge. Adaptive optimizers do not guarantee a global minimum.

Actual parameter updates, up to the configured maximum

Momentum accumulates velocity to smooth changes in direction. Nesterov measures the gradient at a look-ahead location. RMSprop rescales coordinates by recent squared gradients. Adam combines first and second moments with startup bias correction. These are update rules, not substitutes for checking data scale, loss shape or validation performance.

Batch gradients are deterministic on this fixed dataset. Stochastic and mini-batch sampling trade per-update work for noisy estimates. The appropriate rate can differ across methods. A tiny gradient can indicate a local stationary point rather than a good solution.

These rules optimize model parameters in regression and neural training. The two-parameter workbench isolates update behavior, stochasticity and conditioning. A low objective on one task does not rank optimizers universally, and the analytic double well is not an empirical dataset.

Educational two-parameter optimizers, not a general autodiff framework. All calculations run in the browser. No optimizer history is saved automatically. Numerical convergence uses the full gradient norm; noisy methods may reach the budget without satisfying it.

Learned parameters and full BPTT gradient
Gradients below are recomputed on the training set at the current parameters, before clipping. The norm and multiplier above belong to the last applied update.

Why recurrence? A feedforward model receiving only the current independent input cannot know the preceding signal history. A recurrent hidden state carries information from earlier inputs. This tiny scalar architecture is intentionally restrictive; it is not a language model. A single scalar RNN cannot reliably copy an arbitrary previous input while also encoding a new input. The smooth-memory task is better suited to this architecture.

The output derivative is 2(ŷ−y)/(NT). It contributes dy·h to dWy, dy to dby, and dy·Wy to dh. Walk time steps backward and add the future dh before differentiating the current cell. Sum parameter gradients over all time steps and sequences.

Gate preactivation derivatives are dc·c_previous·f(1−f), dc·g·i(1−i), dc·i·(1−g²), and dh·tanh(c)·o(1−o). For each gate q, accumulate dWq=da_q·x, dUq=da_q·h_previous, dbq=da_q. The next backward hidden derivative sums da_q·Uq across gates. Independent gates allow learning what to keep, write and expose.

Full BPTT here has no truncation. Saturating tanh and sigmoid derivatives can shrink gradients. Repeated recurrent multiplication can also enlarge them. Clipping limits an update's norm, but does not solve vanishing gradients. LSTM's additive cell path helps memory when the learned forget gate remains near one, not by guaranteeing unlimited memory.

Applications include sequence regression, sensor streams and short temporal patterns. Limits: synthetic fixed-length task, scalar state, full-batch SGD, no dropout or stacked cells. A lower training loss alone is not evidence of generalization. PyTorch is better suited to larger models and real datasets.
